subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent integrations get an explicit persistent session mode, or should /hooks/agent remain isolated-only with docs clarifying that sessionKey is routing metadata rather than transcript continuity?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting persistent hook sessions changes public hook API/config surface and lets external hook callers re-enter transcript state, so automation cannot safely choose the security/product boundary.

options.title: Accept Explicit Persistent Mode
options.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent/session policy.

options.title: Keep Hooks Isolated-Only
options.body: Reject the persistent-mode direction and update docs to say hook-agent sessionKey values do not provide transcript continuity.

options.title: Pause For Broader Session Identity Design
options.body: Defer the linked PR and define a wider deterministic session identity model for trusted hooks before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Explicit Persistent Mode
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent/session policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter posted the prior product-direction review for this issue and owns the strongest current-line history signal for the affected hook/session path.
